summary: A first-person narrator recounts the aftermath of a traumatic trip to Baalum in the Peten. Sarah has largely forgotten the events, Lou is clinging to her, and the narrator is editing a documentary with David while Steve finishes a photo essay in Belize. The story then turns to the final confrontation with Alex Goddard, who believes he is Shiva, two months after the group returned to the city, which begins as the narrator works late at Applecore.
one_line: Narrator recounts the lingering trauma from Baalum, the fallout for Sarah and Lou, and the final encounter with Alex Goddard.
key_facts: The narrator suffered flashbacks and late-night reveries of forests and children after the Peten trip.
Sarah began sending for re-registration materials from Columbia after she snapped back into her old self.
Sarah seemed to have erased all memories of Baalum, except for occasional mumbles in Kekchi Maya.
Lou had not returned to work and mainly stayed at his Soho place to be near Sarah.
David submitted a very rough cut of Baby Love to the selection committee at Sundance.
The distribution deal with Orion was in temporary turnaround pending another management shuffle.
An advance from Lifetime lowered the heat with Nicky Russo.
Steve returned to Belize to wrap up his photo essay.
Alex Goddard believed he was Shiva, creator and destroyer.
The final confrontation with Alex Goddard occurred two months after the group got back to the city.
The narrator was working late on a Thursday evening in the editing room at Applecore, around seven o'clock.
The narrator was re-cutting new real-life interviews to replace those of Carly and Paula.
Children of Light had gone defunct, and the phone at Quetzal Manor was disconnected.
The replacement interviews were less bubbly than the originals but truer to the realities of adoption.
The narrator had a headache and stomach pains from leftover microwaved pizza.
